question: Slot 7 of the diplomatic actions - the per-class effect. What does accepting an agreement actually change: which fields on which objects, and in what units?

addresses.name: CTradeAction::Apply
addresses.comment:
**CTradeAction slot 7, the per-class effect** - one holder (vftable 0x15FB8D4). 0xA352F0 to the single bare `ret` at 0xA3751B; 4 int3 then CTradeAction slot 12 at 0xA37520, and cfg finds no branch past the ret, so both ends are settled (traps 2 and 3). `this` in ECX, no stack arguments.

Four arms, on `type` (+0x18) and `value` (+0x24), which is the shape every class in the family shares:

- `type == PROPOSE && value`: `GetDefines()->diplomacy->TRADE_INFLUENCE_COST` (+0xA0) subtracted from `countries[actor_id]->diplo_influence` (CCountry +0xA88) at 0xA35B21, clamped at 0 - so **the influence is charged when the offer is made, not when it is accepted**.
- `type == ACCEPT`: `CTradeRoute::IsValid(&this->+0x28)` (0xA4CEE0, the name luabind gives it at 0x8ED468) gates it; then `operator new(0x88)` - `sizeof(CTradeRoute)` - copy-constructed from `this->+0x28` through 0xA4C660, `route->start_date (+0x18) = this->date (+0x1C)`, `route->Activate()` (CRelation slot 10, 0xA4D2C0) which hangs it on both directions' `CDiplomacyStatus::trade_routes` (+0x60), the route appended to the one `CDiplomacy` relation list at `CCurrentGameState +0xB24`, and `CCountry::ChangeRelation(actor, &recipient, TRADE_RELATION_CHANGES)` (+0x9C) at 0xA35F15.
- `value == 0` (a cancellation): TRADE_CANCEL_RELATION_COST (+0xA8) at 0xA369DF.
- then the message: `diplomaticsuccess` or `diplomaticfailure` with `ACTRAWITHUS` / `WETRADEAG` / `OTHERTRADEAG` (accept), `WEBRKTRADE` / `BRKTRADEUS` / `BRKTRADEOTH` (cancel) and `DETRAWITHUS` / `WEDETRA` / `DETRAWITHOTHER` (decline), picked on whether `state->played_country_id (+0xC34)` is the actor, the recipient or neither.

**`this->+0x28` is an embedded CTradeRoute**, which is what IsValid and the copy constructor are both given. The name `Apply` is ours - no string or luabind registration names slot 7 - but the body is read.
addresses.evidence: Extent: `image.decode` to the single ret at 0xA3751B, 4 int3, then CTradeAction slot 12 read straight out of vftable 0x15FB8D4; a scan of every branch in the body finds no target past the ret. Defines: `call 0x445D90` then `[eax+0xBC]` then `[block+0xA0]` / `[block+0x9C]` / `[block+0xA8]`, and `scripts/definesMap.py --block diplomacy` names those three TRADE_INFLUENCE_COST, TRADE_RELATION_CHANGES and TRADE_CANCEL_RELATION_COST - a class reading exactly its own three TRADE_* defines and no others is the check. 0xA4CEE0 is named IsValid by the luabind registration at 0x8ED468 under the CTradeRoute class. Holder count from `vtable.py --holding 0x00A352F0` = 1. Wrong if: the body turned out to be reachable from somewhere other than CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute's slot-7 call (findRefs --callers on 0xA352F0 shows no direct call at all, only the table), or if 0xA4C660 allocated something other than 0x88 bytes.

addresses.name: CNapAction::Apply
addresses.comment:
**CNapAction slot 7** - one holder (vftable 0x15FB754). 0xA2B090 to the bare `ret` at 0xA2C8EA, 5 int3, then CNapAction slot 11 at 0xA2C8F0. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. All four arms read:

- `type == PROPOSE && value`: NAP_JOIN_INFLUENCE_COST (diplomacy +0x54) off `countries[actor_id]->diplo_influence` (+0xA88) at 0xA2B9D3, clamped at 0. Note it is **NAP_JOIN_INFLUENCE_COST and not NAP_INFLUENCE_COST** (+0x20), which this body never reads.
- `type == ACCEPT`: `operator new(0x30)`, `CNap::CNap` (0xA46F00, vftable 0x15FBB68), `nap->first = actor`, `nap->second = recipient`, `nap->start_date (+0x18) = this->date (+0x1C)`, `CNap::Activate()` (slot 10, 0xA471E0) which writes the nap into **both** directions' `CDiplomacyStatus +0x28`, then the nap appended to the `CDiplomacy` relation list at `CCurrentGameState +0xB24` (0xA2BAC8) and `CCountry::ChangeRelation(actor, &recipient, NAP_RELATION_CHANGE)` (+0x4C, 50.0 in BlackICE) at 0xA2BB00.
- `type == DECLINE`: NAP_REJECT_RELATION_CHANGE (+0x58) at 0xA2C40B.
- `value == 0` (breaking a pact): the existing CNap is found in the relation list, `CList_RemoveNode`d (0xA2BF83) and deleted through its slot 0; then **LEAVE_NAP_THREAT_COST (+0x60) passed to 0x4F50A0 by address** (`add edi, 0x60` at 0xA2BFE3, which is why a scan for `mov reg,[block+N]` does not see it - a fourth way a define hides, beside trap 8's three); then LEAVE_NAP_RELATION_CHANGE (+0x4C) and LEAVE_NAP_INFLUENCE_COST (+0x5C).

The message keys are `WENAP` / `THEYNAP` / `OTHERNAP`, `WECANCELNAP` / `THEYCANCELNAP` / `OTHERCANCELNAP` and `WEREJECTNAP` / `THEYREJECTNAP` / `OTHERREJECTNAP` under `diplomaticsuccess` / `diplomaticfailure`. The name `Apply` is ours; the body is read.
addresses.evidence: Extent bounded by CNapAction slot 11 (0xA2C8F0) read out of vftable 0x15FB754, with 5 int3 before it, and no branch target past the ret. Each define identified as `call 0x445D90; mov r,[eax+0xBC]; mov r2,[r+N]` with N resolved through `scripts/definesMap.py --block diplomacy`; the five it reads are exactly the five whose names begin NAP_ or LEAVE_NAP_. The 0x30-byte allocation matches CNap: 0xA46F00 writes vftable 0x15FBB00 (CRelation) then 0x15FBB68 (CNap), both resolved from the RTTI export. The savegame corroborates the object: `nap={ balance=1000.000 our_power=0 their_power=0 first="CHI" second="SOV" start_date="1937.8.21.19" }` inside the one top-level `diplomacy=` block of Ireland1939_01_03_02.hoi3, which is the list at +0xB24. Wrong if: the 0x30 allocation were some other CRelation subclass, or if `[esp+0x24]` at 0xA2BAEE were not `&this->recipient` - the `push ecx` at 0xA2BADB shifts the frame by 4, so it is the slot written at 0xA2BA16 from `this+0x10`.

addresses.name: CShareTechnologyAction::Apply
addresses.evidence: Read instruction by instruction; 42 instructions, two exits, both restoring the same frame, the second reached by `je 0xA4B819` from the entry test. `[eax+0xBC]` off `call 0x445D90` then `[block+0xBC]` = SHARE_TECH_INFLUENCE_COST per `definesMap.py --block diplomacy`. CCountry +0xA88 is `diplo_influence` in project.json and in BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:325 (both halves checked, trap 14). `vtable.py --holding 0x00A4B780` = 1 table. Wrong if: `[esi+0x24]` were not `value` - but project.json already records +0x24 as the action's bool and seven of the family answer slot 18 off it.

addresses.name: CWarGoalBaseAction::Apply
addresses.comment:
**Slot 7 of `CAddWarGoalAction` and `CJoinFactionGoalAction`, and of nothing else** - the two bodies are identical and the linker folded them. Their common base `CWarGoalBaseAction` leaves slot 7 `_purecall`, so neither derived class can own the name and it is put on the base, which is where the code belongs; `vftable_slots` records the slot on both derived classes. 0xA435F0 to the two bare `ret`s at 0xA436B1 and 0xA43770 - one body, the second arm reached by `je 0xA436B2` - 15 int3 after it. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. 0x181 bytes, by far the smallest of the family bar CShareTechnologyAction.

**`this->+0x28` is an embedded `CWarGoal`**: 0x47BBE0 is called with `ECX = this+0x28` and reads `+0x18`/`+0x1C` (the actor tag and index) and `+0xC` (the `CCasusBelliType*`), which is exactly the layout `BiceLib/GameClasses/CWarGoal.hpp` established independently from `CWarGoal::LoadKey`. So `this->+0x34` is that war goal's `casusBelli`.

What it does: with `status = countries[actor_id]->diplomacy[recipient_id]`, it calls 0x651FB0(`status->war` (+0x20), actor tag, actor id) - the add itself, unnamed - then 0x47BBE0 on the war goal, then walks `status->casus_belli` (+0x3C) for the entry whose `+0x24` equals `warGoal->casusBelli->+8`, and on finding it calls 0x649F40(status, 0) and then **removes that CCasusBelli from the `CDiplomacy` relation list at `CCurrentGameState +0xB24` and deletes it through its slot 0**. Reading that as "adding the war goal consumes the casus belli it was justified by" is inference; the removal and the delete are read.

It raises no message and reads no defines (WARGOAL_ADD_COOLDOWN, diplomacy +0xFC, is not read here).
addresses.evidence: `vtable.py --holding 0x00A435F0` prints exactly two tables, CAddWarGoalAction slot 7 (0x15FB454) and CJoinFactionGoalAction slot 7 (0x15FB4B4); CWarGoalBaseAction's own slot 7, read out of vftable 0x15FB2D4, is 0x00B961D5 `_purecall`. Extent: 15 int3 after 0xA43770, and the first arm's `ret` at 0xA436B1 is reached only by falling out of the search loop. The CWarGoal identification is three offsets agreeing with a layout read from a different function in a different session (trap 14's converging-readings case). +0x3C as the casus-belli list is from its writer, CCasusBelli::Activate (0xA47BB0), not from this body. Wrong if: 0x651FB0 turned out not to touch the war, or if `[ebx+0x3C]` were a different list - the test is that CCasusBelli::Activate appends to +0x3C/+0x40/+0x44 on the same `countries[first]->+0xE28[second]` lookup.

addresses.name: CDeclareWarAction::Apply
addresses.comment:
CDeclareWarAction slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB3F4). 0xA12030 to the single bare `ret` at 0xA147B2, 13 int3, then the separate helper 0xA147C0 which this body itself calls twice; CDeclareWarAction slot 11 is further on at 0xA14BB0. 0x2783 bytes, the largest in the family. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments.

Reads its own two defines: WARDEC_WAR_DIPLOMACY_HIT (diplomacy +0x4) at 0xA1281B and WARDEC_INFLUENCE_COST (+0x8) at 0xA1290C. Calls CCountry::RebuildNeighbours (0x4E21E0), 0x4E39C0 and 0x4E70A0 on both sides, 0x4F50A0 (the threat adder), and the war machinery at 0xA4F220 / 0xA506B0 / 0xA51FB0. Its localisation keys are DECLWAR / WEDECLWAR / DECLWAROTHER, DECLWAR_LIMITED, and the four MESS_BADWORDS strings.

**The body was not read instruction by instruction** - the extent, the defines, the call set and the message keys are read; what it writes on CDiplomacyStatus is not. The name `Apply` is ours and is inference from the family, not from this body.
addresses.evidence: Extent from a >=3 int3 run at 0xA147C0 with no branch target past the ret; the next entry is a call target of this very body, so it is a real boundary. Defines by the `GetDefines()->+0xBC->+N` shape resolved through definesMap.py: both names begin WARDEC_, which no other class in the family reads. Holder count 1 from `vtable.py --holding`. Wrong if the name is wrong - which is exactly what `inferred` is saying; nothing here rests on the name.

addresses.name: CAllianceAction::Apply
addresses.comment:
CAllianceAction slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB514). 0xA18D70 to the bare `ret` at 0xA1A434, 11 int3, then CAllianceAction slot 11 at 0xA1A440. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments.

Its four defines are JOIN_ALLIANCE_INFLUENCE_COST (diplomacy +0xC), ALLIANCE_RELATION_CHANGE (+0x40), ALLIANCE_REJECT_RELATION_CHANGE (+0x44) and LEAVE_ALLIANCE_INFLUENCE_COST (+0x10) - the whole ALLIANCE_ group and nothing else. It appends to the `CDiplomacy` relation list at 0xA195DF, which is where the `CAlliance` goes, and calls CCountry::ChangeRelation, CCountry::RebuildNeighbours and 0x4E39C0 on both sides. Keys MILALLACCEPT / MILALLWEACCEPT / MILLALLINVACCEPTOTHER, MILALLBAN*, MILALLREJECT*.

Not read instruction by instruction; the name is inference from the family.
addresses.evidence: Extent bounded by slot 11 out of vftable 0x15FB514 with 11 int3 before it. Four defines by the GetDefines block shape, all four in the ALLIANCE_ group. The relation-list append is the same 0x493E10 call with `esi = state+0xB24` that CNapAction and CTradeAction make. Wrong if the name is wrong; nothing else here depends on it.

addresses.name: CGuaranteeAction::Apply
addresses.comment:
CGuaranteeAction slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB574). 0xA1BCC0 to the bare `ret` at 0xA1D379, 6 int3, then CGuaranteeAction slot 11 at 0xA1D380. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments.

It is the one class whose agreement is **one-sided**: its first test is `this->value`, and on the yes arm it allocates 0x28 bytes, builds a CGuarantee through 0xA46E90 and appends it to the relation list at 0xA1BDCA - all before any `type` test, i.e. a guarantee takes effect on the offer and is not answered. Defines: GUARANTEE_INFLUENCE_COST (diplomacy +0x14), REVOKE_GUARANTEE_RELATION_CHANGE (+0x70), REVOKE_GUARANTEE_INFLUENCE_COST (+0x18). Keys WEGUARAT / GUARATOUS / GUARATOOTHER and GUARACANCELTOTHEM / GUARACANCELTOUS - three perspectives on the grant and two on the revocation, with no accept/decline pair, which is the same conclusion from the other side.

Not read instruction by instruction; the name is inference from the family.
addresses.evidence: Extent bounded by slot 11 out of vftable 0x15FB574. The one-sidedness is read: `cmp byte ptr [esi+0x24], bl; je 0xA1CAD6` is the fourth instruction after the prologue and there is no `cmp [esi+0x18]` before the allocate-and-append at 0xA1BCF5..0xA1BDCA. Its three defines are the whole GUARANTEE_/REVOKE_GUARANTEE_ group. Corroborated from the data side: the savegame's `diplomacy=` block holds 38 `guarantee=` entries, each with `first`, `second`, `start_date` and `end_date`. Wrong if some `type` test sits above it that the straight-line read missed - a cfg pass over the first 0x120 bytes would settle it and was not run.

addresses.name: CInfluenceNation::Apply
addresses.comment: CInfluenceNation slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB5D4). 0xA1E420 to the bare `ret` at 0xA1FB4A, 5 int3, then CInfluenceNation slot 11 at 0xA1FB50. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. Reads DAYS_OF_INFLUENCE_RELATION_CHANGE (diplomacy +0x74) at 0xA1F0EE - a per-day relation drip, not a one-off - and calls 0x503F90, which project.json already describes as the function that cancels a running influence. INFLUENCE_INFLUENCE_COST (+0x30) is **not** read here; the only `GetDefines` reads in the body are +0x74 and one through the inlined getter (`call 0x4452E0` at 0xA1E...), which the block scan cannot follow (trap 8 case 1). Keys WEINFLUENCE / THEYINFLUENCE / OTHERINFLUENCE, with VAL, TIME and UNLIMITED variables. Not read instruction by instruction; the name is inference from the family.
addresses.evidence: Extent bounded by slot 11 out of vftable 0x15FB5D4. The define is the GetDefines block shape; the claim that INFLUENCE_INFLUENCE_COST is not read is a **negative and is marked as such** - the same scan finds +0x74 in this body and finds every other class's own costs, which is its positive control, but it cannot see an inlined GetDefines, and this body contains one. So read that absence as 'not found by this method', not as 'not read'.

addresses.name: CInfluenceAllianceLeader::Apply
addresses.comment: CInfluenceAllianceLeader slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB7B4). 0xA20F70 to the bare `ret` at 0xA21EE1, 14 int3, then CInfluenceAllianceLeader slot 11 at 0xA21EF0; the earlier `ret` at 0xA21027 is an arm of the same frame. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. Reads ALIGN_INFLUENCE_COST (diplomacy +0x7C) at 0xA21165 and DAYS_OF_ALIGN_RELATION_CHANGE (+0x78) at 0xA217D2, and appends to the `CDiplomacy` relation list at 0xA21155 - which is where the `CAlign` goes, and the savegame's `diplomacy=` block holds 8 `align=` entries. Keys WEALIGN / THEYALIGN / OTHERALIGN. Not read instruction by instruction; the name is inference from the family.
addresses.evidence: Extent bounded by slot 11 out of vftable 0x15FB7B4, 14 int3 before it. Two defines by the GetDefines block shape, both in the ALIGN_ group. The append is the same 0x493E10 with `esi = state+0xB24`, and CAlign::Activate (0xA4B110) is the slot 10 that would then be called. Wrong if the name is wrong.

addresses.name: CMilitaryAccessAction::Apply
addresses.comment:
CMilitaryAccessAction slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB634). **Exactly trap 2: 0xA231F0 to the bare `ret` at 0xA247BF, and CMilitaryAccessAction slot 11 begins at 0xA247C0 with no padding at all** - so an int3 scan runs straight past the boundary and gives the body 0x1C90 bytes instead of its real 0x5D0. Taking the longer extent attributes slot 11's tooltip strings (MILACCDESC, CANCELMILACCDESC, DIP_NO_INFL, ISATWAR, ENROUTE) and two further MILACCESS_INFLUENCE_COST reads to slot 7, which is what the first pass here did.

Within the real extent it reads MILACCESS_INFLUENCE_COST (diplomacy +0x2C) twice, MILACC_ACCEPT_RELATION_CHANGE (+0x64) and MILACC_DECLINE_RELATION_CHANGE (+0x68) twice. Keys ACCMILUS / WEACCMIL / ACCMILOTHER, DECMILUS / WEDECMIL / DECMILOTHER, WECANMIL / CANCMILUS / CANMILOTHE. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. Not read instruction by instruction; the name is inference from the family.
addresses.evidence: The boundary is read: 0xA247BF decodes as a one-byte `ret` and `image.read(0xA247C0 - 16, 16)` ends in no 0xCC at all, while vftable 0x15FB634 slot 11 holds 0x00A247C0 exactly. No branch in 0xA231F0..0xA247C0 targets anything past the ret, so it is trap 2 and not trap 3. Defines by the GetDefines block shape, all four MILACC*. Wrong if the name is wrong.

addresses.name: COfferMilitaryAccessAction::Apply
addresses.comment: COfferMilitaryAccessAction slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB694). 0xA25830 to the bare `ret` at 0xA26D05, 10 int3, then COfferMilitaryAccessAction slot 11 at 0xA26D10. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. **It reads no defines at all through `call GetDefines`** - the mirror class of CMilitaryAccessAction, whose own slot 7 carries the MILACC_* costs, so the offer side appears to charge nothing; that is a negative from a scan that cannot see an inlined GetDefines, and this body makes no `call 0x4452E0` either, which is the only extra check run. Keys OFFACCMILUS / WEOFFACCMIL / OFFACCMILOTHER, OFFDECMILUS / WEDECOFFMIL / DECOFFMILOTHER, WECANMIL / CANCMILUS / CANMILOTHE. Not read instruction by instruction; the name is inference from the family.
addresses.evidence: Extent bounded by slot 11 out of vftable 0x15FB694 with 10 int3 before it. The 'no defines' claim has its positive control: the same scan over the other nineteen bodies finds each one's own defines, and over this one finds nothing, and the body contains neither `call 0x445D90` nor `call 0x4452E0`. It could still read a define through a cached global (trap 8 case 2), which was not checked.

addresses.name: CCallAllyAction::Apply
addresses.comment: CCallAllyAction slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB6F4). 0xA27BA0 to the bare `ret` at 0xA29D33, 12 int3, then CCallAllyAction slot 11 at 0xA29D40; the `ret` at 0xA284CE is an arm of the same frame. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. Reads CALLALLY_INFLUENCE_COST (diplomacy +0x1C), WARDEC_WAR_DIPLOMACY_HIT (+0x4) and ALLIANCE_REJECT_RELATION_CHANGE (+0x44) - the only class that borrows two other groups' defines, which fits an ally being dragged into someone else's war. Calls the war machinery (0xA4F220, 0xA506B0) and the faction registries. Keys MILALLHONOUR / WEMILALLHONOUR / OTHERMILALLHONOUR and MILALLDISHONOUR / WEMILALLDISHONOUR / OTHERMILALLDISHONOUR, with VERSUS, VICTIM, FACTION, FACTIONWAROFF and FACTIONWARDEF variables. Note that `CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute` exempts this class alone from the seven-day cooldown write. Not read instruction by instruction; the name is inference from the family.
addresses.evidence: Extent bounded by slot 11 out of vftable 0x15FB6F4 with 12 int3 before it. Defines by the GetDefines block shape. The cooldown exemption is already in project.json's record of 0x60E120 (token 0x309 `callaction`), and 0x309 is CCallAllyAction's own slot-15 token 777, so the two agree. Wrong if the name is wrong.

addresses.name: CEmbargoAction::Apply
addresses.comment:
CEmbargoAction slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB814). 0xA2E5F0 to the bare `ret` at 0xA2F9F0, 15 int3, then CEmbargoAction slot 11 at 0xA2FA00. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. Reads EMBARGO_RELATION_CHANGE (diplomacy +0x80) and EMBARGO_INFLUENCE_COST (+0x28), appends the `CEmbargo` to the relation list at 0xA2EFB9, and calls 0x4F50A0 twice - the threat adder, which is where EMBARGO_THREAT_COST (+0x88) goes. Keys WEEMBARGO / THEYEMBARGO / OTHEREMBARGO and WECANCELEMBARGO / THEYCANCELEMBARGO / OTHERCANCELEMBARGO, with no accept/decline pair: an embargo, like a guarantee, is imposed rather than agreed.

**BlackICE sets EMBARGO_RELATION_CHANGE = -200.0, which times 1000 is exactly the relation floor `[0x1710C38]`** - so one embargo puts the pair at the bottom of the scale in a single step. Not read instruction by instruction; the name is inference from the family.
addresses.evidence: Extent bounded by slot 11 out of vftable 0x15FB814 with 15 int3 before it. Defines by the GetDefines block shape, both EMBARGO_. The floor coincidence is two numbers read independently: `common/defines.lua:299` in this mod says -200.0, and the dword at 0x1710C38, which CCountry::ChangeRelation clamps against, is -200000. Wrong if the name is wrong.

addresses.name: CFactionAction::Apply
addresses.comment: CFactionAction slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB874). 0xA30E70 to the bare `ret` at 0xA32FC6, 9 int3, then CFactionAction slot 11 at 0xA32FD0. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. Its first two tests are read: `this->value` must be set, and `countries[actor_id]->at_war (+0xACC)` must be **clear** - a country at war cannot run a faction action - and then `countries[recipient_id]->faction (+0xD8)->+0x28` must be non-null. Reads INVITE_FACTION_INFLUENCE_COST (diplomacy +0x90) and JOIN_FACTION_INFLUENCE_COST (+0x8C), which is how the one class serves both directions. Keys FACTIONINVITEACCEPT, FACTIONJOINACCEPT / FACTIONJOINACCEPTOTHER, FACTIONJOINDECLINCE, FACTIONINVITEDECLINCE, and the FACTIONCOMMENT_ / FACTIONCOMMENTBAD_ prefixes it builds keys from. Not read instruction by instruction; the name is inference from the family.
addresses.evidence: Extent bounded by slot 11 out of vftable 0x15FB874 with 9 int3 before it. The three entry tests are read straight off 0xA30E9D..0xA30EDF; +0xACC is `at_war` in project.json. Defines by the GetDefines block shape, both FACTION_. Wrong if the name is wrong.

addresses.name: CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::Apply
addresses.comment: CSendExpeditionaryForceAction slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB934). 0xA395B0 to the bare `ret` at 0xA3A853, 12 int3, then CSendExpeditionaryForceAction slot 11 at 0xA3A860. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. Reads EXPEDITION_INFLUENCE_COST (diplomacy +0xAC) and EXPEDITION_RETURN_TIME (+0xB0); EXPEDITION_RECLAIM_TIME (+0xB4) is not read here. It is the only member that reaches into the unit layer - 0x59A190 eleven times, plus 0x4E06F0 / 0x4E0830 / 0x4E0860 and 0x5D3840 - which is consistent with handing brigades over. Keys OUREXPACC, OUREXPDEC, EXPOTHER, with a UNIT variable. Not read instruction by instruction; the name is inference from the family.
addresses.evidence: Extent bounded by slot 11 out of vftable 0x15FB934 with 12 int3 before it. Defines by the GetDefines block shape, both EXPEDITION_. Wrong if the name is wrong.

addresses.name: CLicenceTechnologyAction::Apply
addresses.comment:
CLicenceTechnologyAction slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB994). **A second trap 2 case: 0xA3B5A0 to the bare `ret` at 0xA3CD5D, with only two int3 before CLicenceTechnologyAction slot 11 at 0xA3CD60** - so a scan requiring a run of three or more padding bytes crosses the boundary and gives the body 0x1D20 bytes instead of 0x17C0, which attributes slot 11's LICENCE_INFLUENCE_COST read at 0xA3D13E and its tooltip strings (BUYLICENCEDESC, SELLLICENCEDESC, DIP_NO_INFL, ACT_NO_SELF, ENROUTE) to slot 7.

Within the real extent it reads LICENCE_INFLUENCE_COST (diplomacy +0xB8) once, at 0xA3C36A, and divides through the 64-bit helper 0xB99980 twice - the only member of the family to do arithmetic beyond add-and-clamp, which fits a licence fee. Keys LICBUYACCEPT / LICBUYDECLINE with NAME and NUM variables. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. Not read instruction by instruction; the name is inference from the family.
addresses.evidence: vftable 0x15FB994 slot 11 holds 0x00A3CD60 and `image.read(0xA3CD60 - 16, 16)` ends in exactly two 0xCC - the case the brief's own 'require three int3' rule produces, and the reason the boundary has to come from the table rather than from padding. No branch in the body targets past 0xA3CD5D. The define is the GetDefines block shape. Wrong if the name is wrong.

addresses.name: CDebtAction::Apply
addresses.comment: CDebtAction slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB9F4). 0xA3D8A0 to the bare `ret` at 0xA3E500, 15 int3, then CDebtAction slot 11 at 0xA3E510; the three earlier `ret`s (0xA3DF7B, 0xA3DFDB, 0xA3E29C) are arms of the same frame. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. Reads REVOKE_DEBT_INFLUENCE_COST (diplomacy +0xC8) and ALLOW_DEBT_INFLUENCE_COST (+0xC4); YEARS_TO_REPAY_DEBT (+0xCC) is not read here. Keys DEBTREVOKE, DEBTALLOWACCEPT, DEBTALLOWDECLINE. The smallest of the message-raising members, 0xC61 bytes. Not read instruction by instruction; the name is inference from the family.
addresses.evidence: Extent bounded by slot 11 out of vftable 0x15FB9F4 with 15 int3 before it. Defines by the GetDefines block shape, both DEBT_. Corroborated from the data side: `debtaction_action` is the commonest pending-action key in the save corpus (1,000 blocks), per the transcription note already in FINDINGS-diploaction.md. Wrong if the name is wrong.

addresses.name: CPeaceAction::Apply
addresses.comment: CPeaceAction slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FBA54). 0xA3F710 to the bare `ret` at 0xA40A9B, 4 int3, then CPeaceAction slot 11 at 0xA40AA0; the `ret` at 0xA4085B is an arm of the same frame. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. **It reads no defines at all** - peace costs no influence and moves no relation by a define - and instead calls the war machinery directly: 0xA50440 (`CWar::RemoveAttacker`, already in the record) twice, 0xA51710 (`CWar::RemoveDefender`) twice, 0xA44B10, and 0x4E70A0 / 0x4E7190 on both countries. Keys PEACEACCEPT, PEACEDECLINE, and nothing else - no third-party perspective. Not read instruction by instruction; the name is inference from the family.
addresses.evidence: Extent bounded by slot 11 out of vftable 0x15FBA54. 0xA50440 and 0xA51710 are CWar::RemoveAttacker and CWar::RemoveDefender in project.json, which is what makes 'it ends the war directly' a reading of named calls rather than a guess. The 'no defines' negative has the same positive control as COfferMilitaryAccessAction's: the scan finds every other class's own defines, and this body contains no `call 0x445D90` and no `call 0x4452E0`.

addresses.name: CRequestLendLeaseAction::Apply
addresses.comment: CRequestLendLeaseAction slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB334). 0xA0ECC0 to the bare `ret` at 0xA0FC57, 8 int3, then CRequestLendLeaseAction slot 11 at 0xA0FC60; the three earlier `ret`s are arms of the same frame. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. **It reads ALLOW_DEBT_INFLUENCE_COST (diplomacy +0xC4), not a lend-lease define** - there is no LEND_LEASE_*_INFLUENCE_COST in the block, only LEND_LEASE_NEUTRALITY_LIMIT (+0x100) and the two IC caps (+0x104/+0x108), none of which this body reads. Keys LENDACCEPT, LENDDECLINE, LENDOFFERREFUSED. Not read instruction by instruction; the name is inference from the family.
addresses.evidence: Extent bounded by slot 11 out of vftable 0x15FB334 with 8 int3 before it. The define is `call 0x445D90; mov r,[eax+0xBC]; mov r2,[r+0xC4]` at 0xA0F1B2, and definesMap.py puts ALLOW_DEBT_INFLUENCE_COST at diplomacy +0xC4 - an unexpected answer, which is why it is worth stating; it would be wrong if the block pointer in that register were something other than the diplomacy block, and the register is traced from the `call 0x445D90` three instructions earlier.

addresses.name: COfferLendLeaseAction::Apply
addresses.comment: COfferLendLeaseAction slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB394). 0xA10870 to the bare `ret` at 0xA11573, 12 int3, then COfferLendLeaseAction slot 11 at 0xA11580; the `ret` at 0xA10D4D is an arm of the same frame. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. Reads no defines (same negative, same control as CPeaceAction). Keys LENDOFFERACCEPT, LENDOFFERREFUSED, LENDREVOKE. Not read instruction by instruction; the name is inference from the family.
addresses.evidence: Extent bounded by slot 11 out of vftable 0x15FB394 with 12 int3 before it. No `call 0x445D90` and no `call 0x4452E0` anywhere in the body.

addresses.name: CCountry::ChangeRelation
addresses.signature: void __fastcall CCountry::ChangeRelation(CCountry* this@EDI, CCountryTag* other@ECX, int delta@stack:4)
addresses.evidence: Read instruction by instruction, 24 instructions. 0x402610 is `CCountry* __thiscall CCountryTag::GetCountry(CCountryTag* this)` in project.json, which is what identifies ECX as a CCountryTag* rather than a guess from `[ecx+4]`. CCountry +0xE28 is the diplomacy array in project.json. The two clamp dwords were read out of the image directly: 200000 and -200000. The scale is corroborated three independent ways: the UI range, BlackICE's `EMBARGO_RELATION_CHANGE = -200.0` in common/defines.lua:299 landing exactly on the floor, and definesMap.py's statement that every define in the block is stored x1000. Wrong if: the receiver were not in EDI - every one of the eighteen callers does `mov edi, db->+0x16C[id]` immediately before the call, and the function's first use of EDI is `[edi+0xE28]`, so a caller that did not would fault; or if `+0x38` were not relation, which project.json already asserts from the alignment code's averaging of it.

addresses.name: CNap::Activate
addresses.comment:
**CNap slot 10.** `CRelation` leaves slot 10 `_purecall` and nine of its ten subclasses override it; it is the method that hangs a freshly made relation object on the two countries it is between. This one writes **both** directions' `CDiplomacyStatus +0x28` (`nap`) with `this` and sets `+0x59` on both, then goes on into the inlined game-state accessor. 0xA471E0 to the `ret` at 0xA472FA, 5 int3, then CNap slot 11 at 0xA47300. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments.

Only the first 0x1B bytes of real work were read - the two status writes - not the tail. The name `Activate` is ours and is inference from what the nine bodies have in common.
addresses.evidence: Read: `countries[this->+0xC]->+0xE28[this->+0x14]` and `countries[this->+0x14]->+0xE28[this->+0xC]` both take `+0x59 = 1` and `+0x28 = esi(this)`, at 0xA47226..0xA47250. `+0x28 nap` is already in project.json, described as 'a CRelation subclass', which this confirms from the writer's side. Extent from CNap slot 11 in vftable 0x15FBB68. Holder count 1. The name is inference; the field writes are read.

addresses.name: CGuarantee::Activate
addresses.comment: **CGuarantee slot 10**, 0x61 bytes, 0xA46DB0 to the bare `ret` at 0xA46E10, 15 int3, then CGuarantee slot 11 at 0xA46E20 - read end to end, and the cleanest statement of what slot 10 is for. It writes `this` into **both** directions' `CDiplomacyStatus +0x1C` and sets `+0x59` on both, and does nothing else. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. The name `Activate` is ours.
addresses.evidence: 17 instructions, read end to end, no branch. Both status lookups go through `countries[...]->+0xE28[...]`, the array project.json already names. +0x1C held no name in project.json or in any GameClasses header (both grepped, trap 14). Wrong if +0x1C were something else - the test is that only CGuarantee's slot 10 writes it, and CGuaranteeAction's slot 7 is the only slot 7 that builds a CGuarantee.

addresses.name: CAlliance::Activate
addresses.comment: **CAlliance slot 10.** Writes `this` into both directions' `CDiplomacyStatus +0x14` with `+0x59 = 1` on both, then continues into the inlined game-state accessor. 0xA46A40 to the `ret` at 0xA46BE3, 12 int3, then CAlliance slot 11 at 0xA46BF0. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. Only the status writes were read. The name `Activate` is ours.
addresses.evidence: Writes read at 0xA46A84..0xA46AAE through two `countries[...]->+0xE28[...]` lookups. **Independent agreement:** project.json's comment on 0x8A9390 already says that predicate answers false 'if our own faction leader's CDiplomacyStatus toward them has +0x14 set' - i.e. it reads +0x14 as 'they are our ally', which is what this writer makes it. Two readings converging (trap 14). Extent from CAlliance slot 11 in vftable 0x15C1C38.

addresses.name: CDependency::Activate
addresses.comment: **CDependency slot 10, inherited by CVassal** - two tables, one family (CVassal derives from CDependency and does not override it), so this is inheritance and not a fold. Writes `this` into both directions' `CDiplomacyStatus +0x18` with `+0x59 = 1`, then calls 0x4EDD80 on each country. 0xA47760 to the `ret` at 0xA477F9, 6 int3, then CDependency slot 11 at 0xA47800. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. The save writes these as `vassal=` blocks in the one `diplomacy=` list. Only the status writes were read. The name `Activate` is ours.
addresses.evidence: `vtable.py --holding 0x00A47760` prints CDependency slot 10 and CVassal slot 10, and `hoi3.classes()` gives CVassal's base as CDependency. Writes read at 0xA47790 and 0xA477BB. The savegame's `diplomacy=` block in Ireland1939_01_03_02.hoi3 holds 7 `vassal=` entries, which is the data-side witness that the objects exist and live in that list.

addresses.name: CCasusBelli::Activate
addresses.comment:
**CCasusBelli slot 10**, read end to end, 0xA47BB0 to the `ret` at 0xA47D00 with a second arm exiting at 0xA47D15 - one body, the second reached from 0xA47C8C. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments.

Two gates first, both on `CRelation +0x1C` (the end date): `(end_date - 43800000) / [0x160A550] < 2` returns without doing anything, and so does `end_date < gameState->tick (+0xBDC)` - an expired or nearly expired casus belli is not attached. 43800000 is the null-date epoch the record already knows from `[0x170C2B8]`. Then it appends a 0x10-byte `{this, prev, next, byte}` node to **one** direction's `CDiplomacyStatus` list at `+0x3C` (head) / `+0x40` (tail) / `+0x44` (count), the direction being `countries[this->first_id]->diplomacy[this->second_id]`, and sets `+0x59 = 1`. **This is the list `CWarGoalBaseAction::Apply` searches and consumes from.** The name `Activate` is ours.
addresses.evidence: Read with cfg.py from the entry so the two arms are both covered; 0xA47CB7..0xA47D01 is the append, byte for byte the same shape as CTradeRoute::Activate's append to +0x60/+0x64/+0x68 and as the recorded 0x493E10. The payload is `edi`, and `edi = ecx` at 0xA47BD1, so it is `this` and not something else - worth checking because CTradeRoute's version appends `esi` and CCasusBelli's appends `edi`. Extent from CCasusBelli slot 11 (0xA47D20) in vftable 0x15FBB9C. Wrong if the list were in the other direction: the lookup is `[edi+0xC]` for the array owner and `[edi+0x14]` for the index, which are first.id and second.id respectively.

addresses.name: CInfluence::Activate
addresses.comment:
**CInfluence slot 10.** Unlike the alliance, nap, guarantee and dependency cases it writes **one** direction only - `countries[second_id]->diplomacy[first_id]->+0x2C = this`, i.e. the influenced country's view of the influencer - with `+0x59 = 1`, and it also sets `CCountry +0x1144 = 1` on the influenced country (unnamed). 0xA4AAD0 to the `ret` at 0xA4AC12, then CInfluence slot 7 at 0xA4AC20. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments.

This **refines** `CDiplomacyStatus +0x2C influence_running`, which project.json records as 'non-zero while a diplomatic influence is running between the pair': it is not a flag but the `CInfluence*` itself, and only one side of the pair carries it. Only the status write was read. The name `Activate` is ours.
addresses.evidence: Write read at 0xA4AB3F..0xA4AB4C: `edi = countries[this->+0x14]`, `ecx = edi->+0xE28`, `eax = ecx[this->+0xC]`, `[eax+0x59] = 1`, `[eax+0x2C] = esi(this)`. The existing name in project.json is left alone because it is still right - a non-null pointer is non-zero - so this is a refinement stated here rather than a revision. Extent from CInfluence slot 7 in vftable 0x15FBBD0. Wrong if the two index registers were swapped, which is what the `+0x14` / `+0xC` reading turns on.

addresses.name: CAlign::Activate
addresses.comment: **CAlign slot 10.** Also one-directional, and the opposite way round from CInfluence: `countries[first_id]->diplomacy[second_id]->+0x30 = this`. It does **not** set `+0x59`. It then reads a define and goes on. 0xA4B110 to the `ret` at 0xA4B2DF, with CAlign slot 7 beginning at 0xA4B2E0 **immediately, no padding** - trap 2, and the boundary comes from the table. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. Only the status write was read. The name `Activate` is ours.
addresses.evidence: Write read at 0xA4B176..0xA4B182: `ebx = countries[this->+0xC]`, `ecx = ebx->+0xE28`, `eax = ecx[this->+0x14]`, `[eax+0x30] = esi(this)`. vftable 0x15FBC04 slot 7 holds 0x00A4B2E0, one byte after the ret, which is why the extent is not from padding. The savegame's `diplomacy=` block holds 8 `align=` entries. Wrong if the index registers were swapped.

addresses.name: CEmbargo::Activate
addresses.comment: **CEmbargo slot 10.** Writes `this` into both directions' `CDiplomacyStatus +0x34` - and, unlike every sibling, sets `+0x59` on neither. 0xA4B530 to the `ret` at 0xA4B619, 6 int3, then CEmbargo slot 11 at 0xA4B620. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments. Only the status writes were read. The name `Activate` is ours.
addresses.evidence: Writes read at 0xA4B574 and 0xA4B598, both through `countries[...]->+0xE28[...]`; the first is `countries[second_id]->diplomacy[first_id]` and the second the reverse, so both directions are covered. Extent from CEmbargo slot 11 in vftable 0x15F9FDC. +0x34 held no name in project.json or any GameClasses header. Wrong if +0x34 were something else - the test is that CEmbargo's slot 10 is its only writer among the nine, and CEmbargoAction's slot 7 is the only slot 7 that builds a CEmbargo.

addresses.name: CTradeRoute::Activate
addresses.comment:
**CTradeRoute slot 10**, and the one slot 10 that appends rather than assigns. For **both** directions it sets `+0x59 = 1` and appends a 0x10-byte `{this, prev, next, byte}` node to the pair's `trade_routes` list - head `+0x60`, **tail `+0x64`**, count `+0x68`. 0xA4D2C0 to the `ret` at 0xA4D3F2, then CTradeRoute slot 11 at 0xA4D400. `this` in ECX, no stack arguments.

This settles `+0x64` as the list's tail, which the record did not hold, and confirms `+0x60` / `+0x68` from the writer's side - project.json had them from the Lua accessor and from a count test. Only the first append was read in full; the second is the same shape with the indices swapped. The name `Activate` is ours.
addresses.evidence: 0xA4D2F3..0xA4D32D read instruction by instruction: `ebx = edi->+0x64` (the old tail), `operator new(0x10)`, node `{this, ebx, 0, 0}`, `edi->+0x68` incremented, `edi->+0x64 = node`, and `edi->+0x60 = node` only when the old count was zero - the textbook head/tail/count append, and the same code the recorded 0x493E10 runs over the CDiplomacy list. project.json already names +0x60 trade_routes and +0x68 trade_routes_count, so the agreement is the check; +0x64 was unrecorded. Extent from CTradeRoute slot 11 in vftable 0x15FBD48.

struct_fields.name: alliance
struct_fields.comment: The pair's alliance object, or null. Written in **both** directions by CAlliance::Activate (CRelation slot 10, 0xA46A40), which is reached from CAllianceAction::Apply (slot 7) when an alliance offer is accepted; the same object is appended to the one CDiplomacy relation list at CCurrentGameState +0xB24 and is saved as an `alliance=` block there. Independent agreement: project.json's own account of 0x8A9390 reads +0x14 as 'they are our ally'.
struct_fields.evidence: The write is read at 0xA46A84/0xA46AAE, both through `countries[...]->+0xE28[...]`. Wrong if CAlliance::Activate were not the slot CAllianceAction reaches - the chain is: slot 7 allocates, builds a CAlliance, calls slot 10, appends to the relation list. The save corpus shows 21 `alliance=` blocks in the one `diplomacy=` list.

struct_fields.name: dependency
struct_fields.comment: The pair's overlord/puppet relationship, or null - a CDependency or its subclass CVassal. Written in **both** directions by CDependency::Activate (CRelation slot 10, 0xA47760, inherited by CVassal), which also calls 0x4EDD80 on each country. Saved as a `vassal=` block in the one `diplomacy=` list at CCurrentGameState +0xB24; the save corpus has 7.
struct_fields.evidence: Writes read at 0xA47790 and 0xA477BB. CVassal's base is CDependency per the RTTI export, and `vtable.py --holding 0x00A47760` shows slot 10 of both, so the body is inherited rather than folded. Wrong if +0x18 were some other relation - no other CRelation subclass's slot 10 writes it.

struct_fields.name: guarantee
struct_fields.comment: The pair's guarantee, or null. Written in **both** directions by CGuarantee::Activate (CRelation slot 10, 0xA46DB0), a 17-instruction function that does nothing else. Reached from CGuaranteeAction::Apply (slot 7), which - alone in the family - builds and attaches its object on the `value` test without ever looking at `type`, so a guarantee takes effect when it is offered. Saved as a `guarantee=` block with `first`, `second`, `start_date` and `end_date` in the one `diplomacy=` list; the save corpus has 38.
struct_fields.evidence: CGuarantee::Activate read end to end; the only two writes in it are `+0x59 = 1` and `+0x1C = this`, on the forward and reverse status. Neither project.json nor any BiceLib/GameClasses header held a name at +0x1C (both grepped). Wrong if CGuaranteeAction's slot 7 built something other than a CGuarantee - it allocates 0x28 bytes through 0xA46E90, which is CGuarantee's constructor neighbourhood, and that step was not read in full.

struct_fields.name: align
struct_fields.comment: The alignment drift the array's owner is running against the other country, or null - **one direction only**, written by CAlign::Activate (CRelation slot 10, 0xA4B110) as `countries[first_id]->diplomacy[second_id]->+0x30 = this`, and it is the one slot 10 that does not set `+0x59`. Reached from CInfluenceAllianceLeader::Apply (slot 7), which reads ALIGN_INFLUENCE_COST and DAYS_OF_ALIGN_RELATION_CHANGE. Saved as an `align=` block in the one `diplomacy=` list; the save corpus has 8.
struct_fields.evidence: Write read at 0xA4B182 with the array owner from `this->+0xC` and the index from `this->+0x14`. The one-directionality is the absence of a second write before the function's `ret` at 0xA4B2DF, and the extent there comes from CAlign slot 7 in vftable 0x15FBC04 sitting at 0xA4B2E0 with no padding - so a wrong extent is the way this claim would be wrong, and the table is what rules it out.

struct_fields.name: embargo
struct_fields.comment: The pair's embargo, or null. Written in **both** directions by CEmbargo::Activate (CRelation slot 10, 0xA4B530), which sets `+0x59` on neither side. Reached from CEmbargoAction::Apply (slot 7), which reads EMBARGO_RELATION_CHANGE and EMBARGO_INFLUENCE_COST and has no accept/decline pair in its message keys: an embargo is imposed, not agreed.
struct_fields.evidence: Writes read at 0xA4B574 and 0xA4B598, both through `countries[...]->+0xE28[...]`, one each way. +0x34 held no name in project.json or in any GameClasses header. No embargo exists in any of the 45 saves, so the data side is silent here - which is stated rather than rounded up.

struct_fields.name: casus_belli
struct_fields.comment: The casus belli the array's owner holds against the other country - **one direction only**, `countries[first_id]->diplomacy[second_id]`. Head at +0x3C, tail at +0x40, count at +0x44, nodes 0x10 bytes `{payload, prev@+4, next@+8, byte@+0xC}`. Written by CCasusBelli::Activate (CRelation slot 10, 0xA47BB0), which refuses to attach one whose end date (CRelation +0x1C) is in the past or within two of whatever `[0x160A550]` divides by. **This is the list CWarGoalBaseAction::Apply (slot 7 of CAddWarGoalAction and CJoinFactionGoalAction) searches**, matching a list entry's +0x24 against the action's own war goal's `casusBelli->+8`, and then removes that CCasusBelli from the CDiplomacy relation list and deletes it.
struct_fields.evidence: The append is read at 0xA47CB7..0xA47D01, the same head/tail/count shape as CTradeRoute::Activate's and as the recorded 0x493E10. The reader is read at 0xA4365C..0xA4369E. Wrong if the payload were not a CCasusBelli: the payload register is `edi`, set from `ecx` at 0xA47BD1 on entry, so it is `this`. No casus_belli block appears in any of the 45 saves, so there is no data-side check.

struct_fields.name: casus_belli_end
struct_fields.comment: Tail of the casus-belli list at +0x3C. Read as the previous node and overwritten with the new one by CCasusBelli::Activate at 0xA47CB7 and 0xA47CE2.
struct_fields.evidence: Read off the append at 0xA47CB7/0xA47CE2. Wrong if the list's fields were ordered differently - the shape is fixed by the `if (oldCount == 0) head = node; else oldTail->next = node` at 0xA47CE8..0xA47D01, which is what distinguishes head from tail.

struct_fields.name: casus_belli_count
struct_fields.comment: How many casus belli the array's owner holds against the other country; the count of the list at +0x3C, incremented by CCasusBelli::Activate at 0xA47CDC and used there to tell the first append from the rest.
struct_fields.evidence: Read off the append at 0xA47CDC..0xA47CE5. Wrong if it were a tail rather than a count - it is `lea edx, [ecx+1]` on the old value, which a pointer would not be.

struct_fields.name: changed
struct_fields.comment: Set to 1 by everything that changes the pair's standing: CCountry::ChangeRelation (both directions, 0x4E65D8 and 0x4E660B) and seven of the nine CRelation::Activate bodies - CNap, CGuarantee, CAlliance, CDependency, CCasusBelli, CInfluence and CTradeRoute. CAlign's and CEmbargo's do not set it. **No reader was looked for**, so the name says what the writers have in common and nothing about what it is for; a dirty flag for the diplomacy screen is a guess and is not recorded as anything more.
struct_fields.evidence: Eleven writes read, each one `mov byte ptr [status+0x59], 1` immediately beside a write of the relation or of a relation-object pointer on the same status. Wrong in the way trap 14's `tutorial_active` was wrong: a name fitted to writers alone. The check that would settle it is a reader scan, which was not run, and that is why this is `inferred`.

struct_fields.name: trade_routes_end
struct_fields.comment: Tail of the `trade_routes` list at +0x60, between it and `trade_routes_count` at +0x68. Read as the previous node and overwritten with the new one by CTradeRoute::Activate (0xA4D2F3 and 0xA4D31E), which appends the route to both directions' lists when a trade offer is accepted.
struct_fields.evidence: Read off the append at 0xA4D2F3..0xA4D32D, which is the head/tail/count shape with +0x60 head, +0x64 tail, +0x68 count - and project.json already names +0x60 and +0x68 those two things, so the middle field is fixed by them. Wrong if +0x68 were not the count, which the record already establishes from a separate test site.

struct_fields.name: relations
struct_fields.comment: **Head of the single polymorphic list of every CRelation in the game** - it is the list inside the embedded CDiplomacy at +0xB24, whose own fields sit at +8 (head), +0xC (tail) and +0x10 (count), which is why one helper is passed +0xB24 and the other +0xB2C. Every `type == ACCEPT` arm of the diplomatic actions' slot 7 appends its freshly made agreement here through 0x493E10 with the owner in ESI (five call sites: 0xA195DF alliance, 0xA1BDCA guarantee, 0xA21155 align, 0xA2BAC8 nap, 0xA2EFB9 embargo, 0xA35ED3 trade), and a cancellation finds its object here and takes it out with CList_RemoveNode before deleting it. This is what the savegame writes as the one top-level `diplomacy=` block: in Ireland1939_01_03_02.hoi3 it holds 1,248 `trade`, 38 `guarantee`, 21 `alliance`, 21 `influence`, 8 `align`, 8 `nap` and 7 `vassal` entries - seven of CRelation's ten subclasses, with CCasusBelli, CEmbargo and CWarning simply absent from that game.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x493E10 read end to end: nodes are 0x10 bytes `{value, prev, next, byte}`, head `[esi+8]`, tail `[esi+0xC]`, count `[esi+0x10]`, and the callers do `lea esi, [state+0xB24]`. CList_RemoveNode (already recorded) is called at 0xA2BF83 with `esi = state+0xB2C`, i.e. the head field itself, which is the cross-check on the +8 offset. The save's block names map one-to-one onto the RTTI subclass list of CRelation. Wrong if +0xB24 were not a CDiplomacy - project.json and BiceLib/GameClasses/CCurrentGameState.hpp:57 both already say it is.

struct_fields.name: relations_end
struct_fields.comment: Tail of the relation list at +0xB2C - the CDiplomacy's own +0xC. Written by 0x493E10 on every append.
struct_fields.evidence: `[esi+0xC]` in 0x493E10 with `esi = state+0xB24`. Wrong if the list fields were ordered otherwise, which the `if (oldCount == 0) head = node; else oldTail->next = node` tail at 0x493E47 settles.

struct_fields.name: relations_count
struct_fields.comment: How many CRelation objects exist - the CDiplomacy's own +0x10. Incremented by 0x493E10 on every append and used there to tell the first append from the rest.
struct_fields.evidence: `lea ebx, [ecx+1]` on `[esi+0x10]` at 0x493E3D. Wrong if it were a pointer, which the increment rules out.

struct_fields.name: relations
struct_fields.comment: The same field as CCurrentGameState +0xB2C - CCurrentGameState derives from CGameState and adds nothing at this offset, so the record carries both, as it already does for +0xB24 `diplomacy`. Head of the single polymorphic list of every CRelation in the game, inside the embedded CDiplomacy at +0xB24 (head at its +8, tail +0xC, count +0x10). Saved as the one top-level `diplomacy=` block.
struct_fields.evidence: Same reading as the CCurrentGameState entry; the duplication follows project.json's existing practice for +0xB24, +0xB3C and +0xB5C, which it records on both structs with the same comment.

struct_fields.name: relations_end
struct_fields.comment: Tail of the relation list at +0xB2C. The same field as CCurrentGameState +0xB30.
struct_fields.evidence: Same reading as the CCurrentGameState entry.

struct_fields.comment: How many CRelation objects exist. The same field as CCurrentGameState +0xB34.
